app.desc: A storybook Mars mission for kids aged 7-12: keep 4 astronauts safe for 10 sols through a real space storm from NASA DONKI data.
top.aiTitle: All pictures were drawn in code by an AI assistant (Claude).

intro.1.title: Hello, Commander!
intro.1.p1: You run a base on Mars.
intro.1.p2: A day on Mars is called a sol.
intro.1.rovi: Hi! I'm Rovi, your robot helper.
intro.2.title: Meet your crew
intro.2.p2: Each one cares for one job.
intro.3.title: A real space storm
intro.3.p1: NASA recorded real space storms (solar flares) on the Sun.
intro.3.p2: Each level replays 10 real days of one of them.
intro.3.p3: The light delay, the warnings and the storm pieces all come from NASA records.
intro.4.title: Share your power
intro.4.p1: You get {power} power points each sol.
intro.4.p2: Air, food and the shield all need power.
intro.4.p3: If something runs out, the mission stops.
quiz.hintPre: Just guess. It's OK not to know yet!
quiz.1.q: One astronaut breathes about 0.84 kg of oxygen each day. There are 4 astronauts. How much oxygen do they need each day?
quiz.2.q: In a space storm (solar flare), what can hurt astronauts on Mars the most?
quiz.2.a0: Tiny, fast pieces from the Sun (protons)
quiz.3.q: The base has only a little power. What happens if you give ALL of it to the shield?
quiz.3.a2: Less air and less food are made

fact.sep: The light from a space storm (solar flare) does not hurt the crew. The tiny, fast pieces that come after it (protons) do. On 20 May 2024, a storm from the Sun reached Mars. NASA's Curiosity rover measured about {ugy} micrograys. That is like 30 chest X-rays!
fact.limit: NASA has a safety limit. In a whole career, an astronaut may get at most {career} mSv of radiation. Today your shield made the storm dose smaller: from {raw} to {dose} mSv.
fact.o2low: Air math: 1 astronaut breathes about {o2} kg of oxygen a day. That is a bit less than a 1-liter bottle of water weighs. 4 × {o2} = {need} kg. Today your machine made only {made} kg.
fact.water: On the Space Station, NASA cleans and reuses {pct} of every 100 drops of water, even sweat! Today, with less power, your base reused only {rec} of 100.
fact.delay: Right now Mars is {min} light-minutes from Earth. A radio message takes that long to arrive, and a rocket would take about {m1} to {m2} months. That is why the crew must solve problems alone.
fact.osdr: Scientists measured the bodies of the 4 Inspiration4 space travelers (2021). More than 95 of every 100 changes went back to normal within a few months after landing. (NASA Open Science Data Repository)
fact.base: Mars gives a little radiation every day, even with no storm: {dose} mSv. NASA's Curiosity rover measured this. So far that adds up to {total} mSv.
fact.o2: Air math: 4 astronauts × {o2} kg = {need} kg of oxygen each sol. Today your machine made {made} kg.

teacher.weekInfo: {flares} flare reports and {seps} SEP records (SEP per sol: {per}). Light delay {min} min ({au} AU, computed from NASA JPL orbit formulas). Earth warnings: {warns}. Raw API responses: data/raw/{id}/.
teacher.fallback: Note: the FLR endpoint returned an error, so DONKI notifications were used for the same flare reports.
ds.cme: DONKI CME (coronal mass ejections: clouds of Sun material)
teacher.sunNote: The Sun today panel calls api.nasa.gov (DONKI notifications type=FLR and SEP, last 7 days, DEMO_KEY) live. If that fails it shows the saved snapshot from {start} to {end}, clearly labeled as archived.
teacher.chars: The astronauts (Aylin, Kofi, Mei, Leo) and Rovi the robot are made-up characters.
teacher.pics: All pictures are drawn in code by an AI assistant (Claude). No photos and no NASA logos are used.
teacher.font: Font: Mali (SIL Open Font License 1.1), stored with the game so all Azerbaijani letters show.
teacher.sourcesNote: Source titles are kept in their original language.
caveat.0: DONKI flares are observed by GOES from Earth orbit. Flare class (C/M/X) is peak X-ray brightness at Earth, not radiation dose at Mars. The game uses SEP (proton) records for dose and flare class only as context.
caveat.1: DONKI notifications only report flares of about M5.0 and above, so smaller flares are not included.
caveat.2: Earth's warnings use the flares/CMEs that DONKI itself links to each SEP record. If the blast and the particles are on the same day, the game says the warning came too late.
caveat.3: The light delay is computed for the middle of each storm week from approximate orbit formulas.
caveat.flr404: The DONKI FLR endpoint returned an error when the data was fetched, so DONKI notifications (type=FLR) were used for the same flare reports.
ref.mars_surface_dose_msv_per_day: Average radiation dose on the Mars surface (Curiosity RAD, Gale crater)
ref.o2_kg_per_crew_per_day: Oxygen used per astronaut per day
ref.iss_water_recovery_pct: Water recovered by ISS life support after the Brine Processor Assembly (93-94% before it)
ref.sep_event_dose_limit_msv: Short-term limit for one solar particle event
ref.curiosity_rad_2024_05_20_ugy: Dose Curiosity RAD measured on Mars during the 20 May 2024 storm (about 30 chest X-rays)
ref.mars_trip_months: Shortest typical trip from Earth to Mars (7 to 10 months)
ref.mars_trip_months_max: Longer typical trip from Earth to Mars
ref.osdr_inspiration4_recovery_pct: Inspiration4: share of measured body markers back to normal within months after the flight
rule.power.v: {power} points (never enough for all three systems at full level)
rule.ls.v: each power level makes {perLevel} kg O2, so level 2 covers 4 × 0.84 kg exactly
rule.water.k: Water recycling by Life Support level
rule.water.v: 0: 0%, 1: 93%, 2-3: 98% (the ISS values before and after the brine processor). A full tank lasts 4 sols with no recycling.
rule.food.v: food packs (1 pack = food for 1 astronaut for 1 day). Start {start}, each greenhouse level grows {per}, the crew eats {need} per sol, store max {max}
rule.dose.v: {perSep} mSv per DONKI SEP record on that date if unshielded. Real Mars storm doses vary a lot.
rule.shield.v: levels 1/2/3 cut the storm dose by 40% / 70% / 90%. The everyday 0.64 mSv/day is not cut.
rule.limit.v: {limit} mSv for this exercise (game rule, far below NASA's 600 mSv career limit)
rule.sol.v: 1 sol = 1 real UTC date of the storm week (a real sol is 24 h 39 min)
rule.mystery.v: picks one of {n} real DONKI storm weeks at random; the date is revealed at the end
rule.sci.v: calm sols only: costs 1 of the 5 power points and earns 1 star. Rank: survived = Bronze, {silver}+ stars = Silver, {gold}+ stars = Gold
rule.warn.v: shown the sol before a storm day if DONKI links that storm's SEP records to a flare/CME on an earlier day; otherwise the game says the warning came too late
rule.advice.v: the answer arrives on the next sol, based on what the base looked like when you asked
mission.heli.title: Fly the helicopter
mission.heli.fact: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter made 72 flights on Mars (2021 to 2024). It was the first powered flight on another planet.
mission.moxie.title: Make oxygen from Martian air
mission.moxie.fact: Perseverance's MOXIE machine made 122 grams of oxygen from Mars air. That is about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.
mission.clouds.title: Photograph Martian clouds
mission.clouds.fact: On 2 February 2023, the Curiosity rover took the first clear photo of sun rays shining through clouds on Mars.
mission.sample.title: Collect a rock sample
mission.sample.fact: A sample is a small piece of rock kept for study. Perseverance seals rock cores in tubes so a future mission could bring them to Earth.
mission.rad.title: Measure the radiation
mission.rad.fact: Curiosity's RAD tool has measured radiation on Mars since 2012. Our 0.64 mSv per day comes from RAD.
mission.weather.title: Check the Mars weather
mission.weather.fact: Curiosity's weather station (REMS) measures air temperature, air pressure and wind in Gale crater.
